Research supports separating item relevance, relative preference, and list redundancy: [Beyond Binary Relevance](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/beyond-binary-relevance-preferences-diversity-set-level-judgments/) discusses pairwise preferences and set-level novelty judgments. An actionable adaptation is a multilabel taxonomy: immediate choice, explicitly deferred relevance, specific-match ranking inversion, explicit incompatibility, explicit duplication, explicit disinterest, and insufficient information. Measure ranking inversions only for explicitly preferred pairs; compute compatibility/duplication objection rates among assessable recommendations. These are proposed operational definitions, not an established taxonomy. Nonselection alone cannot establish disinterest or deferred relevance. Titles/descriptions can establish item attributes; histories/timestamps establish observed interactions, without proving ownership, current intent, or compatibility.

Annotation reliability requires clear definitions, examples, independent annotation, and disagreement review. [Artstein and Poesio](https://aclanthology.org/J08-4004/) survey chance-corrected agreement measures; [Oortwijn et al.](https://aclanthology.org/2021.humeval-1.15/) describe systematic disagreement resolution. Report agreement before adjudication, per-label counts, and an appropriate coefficient such as Krippendorff’s alpha; retain evidence spans and distinguish subjective disagreement from missing evidence. Leave unsupported preferences and unidentified items unassessable.

[Selective classification](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.08500) formalizes the trade-off between error on accepted predictions and coverage. Adapt this principle to diagnostic annotation: report assessable fraction, abstention reasons, and error/objection rates conditional on assessment, with denominators and category breakdowns. Otherwise, improved diagnostic scores may merely reflect excluding difficult items. Keep these diagnostics separate from the fixed macro validation HR@10; abstention must not remove benchmark users or candidates.
